Third-party components used by drawing, identity and initial-geometry adapters

Chemistry Development Kit (CDK) 2.12 — GNU LGPL 2.1 or later.
https://github.com/cdk/cdk
Copyright notices are retained in the accompanying source archives and cdk-NOTICE.txt.
License text: LGPL-2.1.txt (and GPL-2.0.txt).
Modules: cdk-sdg, cdk-silent, cdk-atomtype, cdk-core, cdk-ctab,
cdk-interfaces, cdk-io, cdk-ioformats, cdk-isomorphism, cdk-smiles,
cdk-standard, cdk-valencycheck, cdk-builder3d, cdk-forcefield, cdk-data.

Beam 1.3.10 — BSD 2-Clause.
Copyright (c) 2013, European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI).
https://github.com/johnmay/beam
Full notice and terms: beam-NOTICE.txt. Modules: beam-core, beam-func.

Vecmath 1.5.2 — GPL version 2 with the Classpath exception.
Copyright 1998–2008 Sun Microsystems, Inc. All rights reserved.
https://github.com/hharrison/vecmath
Full license and exception: vecmath-LICENSE.txt; notice: vecmath-NOTICE.txt.

The above libraries are unmodified. Their exact published Maven source JARs
are included under META-INF/quantum-third-party/sources in the application JAR.
Use the JDK jar tool or any ZIP reader to extract this directory. Individual
source files retain their original author notices and license terms.

To rebuild or relink the adapter, use the Quantum IR Studio source checkout,
JDK 25 and Maven. The dependencies are declared in quantum-chemistry-drawing/pom.xml;
replace their versions with locally installed compatible modified artifacts as needed.
Run Maven with -pl quantum-desktop -am package. The resulting desktop JAR includes
the selected dependency classes and service registrations. The source-copy build
step includes matching dependency source archives and fails if they are unavailable.
No library chemical model is persisted. Adapters return 2D depictions and bounded
initial 3D candidates with independent stereochemical verification to the existing
Quantum chemistry core. CDK initial candidates are not optimized structures or measured facts.
Core calculations and QCHEM data use the core.

Initial 3D template construction runs in a separate bounded JVM using the same
packaged libraries; the application verifies atom mapping and stereochemistry
from returned coordinates before accepting them. Library source is unmodified.

OpenChemLib 2026.10.1 — BSD 3-Clause.
Copyright (c) 1997–2016 Actelion Pharmaceuticals Ltd.; author notices are retained in its source archive.
https://github.com/Actelion/openchemlib
Full license and copyright notice: openchemlib-LICENSE.txt.
The bundled smile package retains Apache License 2.0; full terms: openchemlib-smile-LICENSE.txt.
The exact published openchemlib-2026.10.1-sources.jar is included with the source archives.
OpenChemLib is unmodified. Its old JavaFX dependencies are excluded.
Conformer generation uses its ring-fragment and torsion sampling, followed by MMFF94s+
minimization (vacuum, dielectric 1, non-bonded cutoff 100 angstrom). Only converged
local minima with independent atom-mapping/geometry/stereochemistry checks are returned.
These model energies are not physical measurements, free energies, or a guarantee of
the global minimum. Missing atom parameters or unsupported stereo produce diagnostics.
Hydrogens needed internally are not added to the persisted source graph. The bounded
worker JVM is terminated on cancellation/deadline; no new library chemical model is stored.
